name: Condition-number-bounded geometric decay predictor for iterative Laplacian-type refinement (ICP error-scale replacement for a fitted log-linear model)

statement.latest: \kappa_k=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(H_k)}{\lambda_2(H_k)},\quad \rho_k\le\frac{\kappa_k-1}{\kappa_k+1}\ (\text{standard Gauss--Newton/ICP normal-equation contraction rate}),\quad s_{k,i}:=\rho_k^{\,K-k}\cdot|\text{residual}_{k,i}|\ \text{(replacing the fitted log-linear }s_{k,i}\text{ of weld/M.61? / task-conditioned-6d-pose-stop's C6)}
statement.note_ascii: kappa_k = lambda_max(H_k)/lambda_2(H_k) of the ICP normal-equations matrix at stage k; rho_k <= (kappa_k-1)/(kappa_k+1) bounds the per-stage contraction rate (standard optimization theory, cited not re-derived here); s_k,i = rho_k^(K-k) * current residual replaces the ad hoc log-linear fit with a decay law derived from the actual conditioning of the problem

parents.evidence: H_k, the ICP normal-equations matrix at each refinement stage, is treated as an instance of the same weighted-graph-Laplacian-type quadratic-form object L_R already roots -- this identification is itself an assumption of this proposal, not an established Toledo fact, and must be checked against the real backend's H_k before use (see honest_caveats).
supplies a proven, axiom-free upper bound on lambda_max(H_k) (Anderson-Morley curvature ceiling)
alternative proven upper bound on lambda_max(H_k) (Rayleigh-quotient degree bound), whichever is tighter for the real correspondence graph is used

supplies the lower bound on lambda_2(H_k) via the diameter-based algebraic-connectivity floor lambda_2>=4/(nD) -- this citation is currently coq_status wrapped_related (cited, not itself mechanized in Toledo); a Coq witness is being attempted as part of this proposal, see coq field once it lands.

honest_caveats: STATUS CORRECTED 2026-09-11: this entry's status field previously read 'unverified' with resistance_evidence still saying 'not yet run', even though the fourth real-data cycle (task-conditioned-6d-pose-stop, run 4, 2026-09-09) already executed and STRUCTURALLY REFUTED this proposal -- the real ICP correspondence-graph Hessian H_k was found to have no graph-diameter structure, so q_formal/M.07's diameter-based floor lambda_2>=4/(nD) does not apply to it at all (the H_k~L_R identification flagged as an assumption below is the specific thing that failed). This mislabeling was caught and fixed during a Toledo debt sweep (founder instruction: 'ติดป้ายที่ถูกปฏิเสธไปแล้วด้วยนะ' -- also tag items that have already been refuted). Status corrected to 'refuted_structural'; see lab/results/real-bop-lmo-2026-09-09-run4/RESULT.md in task-conditioned-6d-pose-stop for the full result.

The identification of ICP's normal-equations matrix H_k with the combinatorial graph Laplacian L_R family is an ANALOGY, not a proven equivalence -- H_k is built from point-correspondence covariances (a weighted least-squares Hessian), not literally the unweighted-degree-minus-adjacency object L_R:=D_W-W. This proposal's parents[] instance_of edge records this as an assumption to be checked, not an established fact.

The Gauss-Newton contraction-rate formula rho_k<=(kappa_k-1)/(kappa_k+1) is a standard, cited result from numerical optimization (not re-derived or Coq-verified here); it also assumes local, well-behaved convergence (no line-search failures, no degenerate correspondences), which real noisy depth data may violate.

q_formal/M.07's lambda_2>=4/(nD) bound requires knowing the correspondence graph's diameter D and vertex count n at each stage -- these must be computed from the real backend's actual correspondence structure, not assumed.

This is a genuinely higher-risk hypothesis than the prior two real-data cycles (tolerance re-derivation, Bonferroni checkpoints), both of which only touched calibration machinery; this one touches the pose ERROR ESTIMATE itself and could be wrong in either direction (tighter AND correct, tighter AND WRONG/uncalibrated, or no different from the log-linear fit).

The floor q_formal/M.07.v1 (lambda_2>=4/(nD)) shrinks toward zero as the correspondence graph n/diameter D grow -- combined with the ceiling weld/M.40/42, this gives kappa<=O(nD), which is NOT uniform in graph size. Expect rho_k=(kappa-1)/(kappa+1) to worsen (slower contraction) as the real correspondence graph gets denser, not to stay fixed -- this is the same phenomenon behind why the continuum Navier-Stokes regularity problem is hard (see docs/NAVIER_STOKES_THROUGH_OUR_LENS.md), read through this workspace's own discrete lens, not a defect introduced by this proposal.
